title: Doorbell Predicts Rewards — activity cover
note:
Cover: everything essential inside the middle 75% of the width, because the library card and the map rail crop it to a centred square. A hand resting flat on her chest is the calm-greeting picture; a hand hooked into her collar is restraint, which is a different lesson and the one a generic prompt draws. It is also the fallback sheet for two activities, so it lands in the 16:7 Today band as well as the square. docs/pilot-prompts.md: every cover that passed that band first time has a crouching or kneeling human, because a standing adult does not fit in 58% of the height.

Round 35 got every content claim right and was cut in the Today band: the handler's head began 7.8% down a frame whose 16:7 band starts at 17.5%, so her crown was sliced off on the app's largest surface. The spec had already named the middle-60%-of-height rule and given the reason, and that was not enough — the same thing happened on door-stay-cover, where naming a percentage failed three times. What has worked instead, on door-sound-03-name-distant and the handle rung, is stating the drawn SIZE and the empty margins rather than the safe area: a figure told to be smaller gets smaller, a figure told to stay inside a band gets moved. Re-declared for cool-flat-v2 (the plaster wall) on 2026-09-04; 2 mention(s) of the old room moved to the new hexes and wording.
scene: The entry hall, near the closed charcoal front door but with the door pushed to the edge of the frame — this is a portrait of the pair, not of the door. The handler kneels on one knee so her face is level with Lucy's, the two of them close together and turned toward each other, near enough that a square crop of the middle of the picture holds both faces comfortably. Her near hand rests open and flat on Lucy's chest, below the collar — the palm laid against the fur, fingers relaxed and pointing down. It is a resting touch, not a hold: no finger is hooked under the collar, she is not gripping the fur, and there is no tension anywhere in the arm. Lucy sits square, leaning very slightly toward her, ears soft, mouth closed, looking at the handler's face. The black leash is clipped to the collar ring and drops away slack out of the bottom of the frame; give it a thin lighter outline where it passes near her coat, and keep it off her back and shoulders. HOW BIG THE PAIR IS DRAWN, which is the constraint this cover keeps failing: draw them SMALLER than the composition wants. The top of the handler's head sits about a QUARTER of the way down from the top edge of the picture and no higher, and the lowest thing that matters — her forward knee and foot — no lower than three quarters of the way down. Above both heads there is a clear band of empty plaster wall at least a fifth of the picture's height with nothing in it, and below them clear empty floor. Left and right, nothing that matters enters the outer eighth of the width. The reason is that the app crops this picture two ways at once: to a wide Today band that keeps only the middle strip of the HEIGHT, and to a centred square that keeps only the middle three-quarters of the WIDTH. A head near the top edge is decapitated in the Today band. It is better to have empty wall above them than a cover with the top of a head sliced off. Background: the plaster wall, one baseboard line, a sliver of the closed door at the edge. No guest, no doormat, no bed.
mustBeTrue: the top of the handler's head sits about a quarter of the way down the frame with a clear band of empty wall above both heads, and nothing that matters falls in the top fifth, the bottom quarter or the outer eighth of either side — so neither the wide Today band nor the centred square clips a head; the handler's hand lies flat and open against Lucy's chest below the collar with no finger hooked under it and no grip on the fur, the two faces are level with each other, and Lucy sits square and relaxed looking at the handler's face.
